literal: Than begging, is painful indeed, accumulated things oneself alone as a solitary person eating.
translation: Eating one's hoarded wealth all by oneself is truly more painful than begging.
modern: தான் சேர்த்து வைத்த பொருளைத் தான் மட்டுமே தனியாக இருந்து உண்பது, பிறரிடம் சென்று பிச்சை எடுப்பதை விட மிகவும் துன்பமானது.
explanation: This couplet compares the pain of begging with the act of hoarding wealth to consume it alone. The word 'இரத்தலின்' uses the ablative suffix to mean 'worse than begging', setting up a stark comparison. 'நிரப்பிய' refers to things that have been amassed or filled up over time. To eat these accumulated things entirely by oneself, expressed by the phrase 'தாமே தமியர் உணல்' (oneself as a solitary person eating), is declared to be 'இன்னாது' (painful or bad). The particle 'மன்ற' adds certainty, emphasizing that selfish hoarding without sharing is truly a more wretched state than being forced to beg.
